GM.thesis_one_line: America's #2 automaker is cheap on cash flow (8.5-14% free-cash-flow yield, automotive net cash $3.7bn, implied growth below zero on every cash base), but the raised guidance is on adjusted measures only, EV charges are rising rather than shrinking, and the margin of safety is smaller than first shown.
kill_criteria: Adjusted EBIT-adjusted guidance cut (vs the current $14.0–16.0bn FY26 range) at any of the next two quarterly releases.
Automotive segment swings from net-cash to net-debt positive (i.e., Automotive debt exceeds Automotive cash+securities) for two consecutive quarters.
Gross tariff-cost estimate re-raised above the current $2.5–3.5bn 2026 range.

Two consecutive quarters of GAAP-to-adjusted EBIT gap driven by *new* (not previously disclosed) restructuring/impairment charges exceeding $1bn/quarter. [Fired as of Q2 2026, RA12: EV strategic-realignment charges were $1,077m in Q1 2026 and $2,279m in Q2 2026 (plus China $177m), against $1.0bn guided for the full year in the previous guidance; the full-year adjustments guide moved from $1.0bn to $3.5bn.]
China equity income (currently modestly positive, $83M in Q2 2026) turns negative for two consecutive quarters.

Automotive debt including IPU obligations (up to $4.5bn, 8-K 11 Aug 2026) exceeds automotive cash and marketable securities for two consecutive quarters on a reported basis (added 6 Oct 2026, RA12; the Q2 2026 net cash is $3.67bn).

Cash adjustments between reported and adjusted automotive free cash flow exceed $1bn in either Q3 or Q4 2026 (full-year guide $4.1bn equals the H1 actual of about $4.1bn, so none is guided for H2) (added 6 Oct 2026, RA12).
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 GAAP diluted EPS was $3.27 vs the original guidance range of $8.30-9.05, due to a $7.2bn Q4 2025 EV-realignment charge.
China JV restructuring charges are recurring ($99M six-month 2026).
Cruise robotaxi business was wound down after >$10bn cumulative spend (Dec 2024) - a past capital-allocation miss.
Automotive-only balance sheet split and TTM adjusted-EBIT reconstruction were derived via automated summarization of primary SEC documents, not a full manual read of every table.

Guidance quality (Q2 2026 release): EBIT-adjusted, adjusted EPS and adjusted automotive FCF were raised, but GAAP net income guidance was cut to $8.4-9.8bn from $9.9-11.4bn, diluted EPS to $8.98-10.98 from $10.62-12.62 and automotive operating cash flow to $15.4-19.4bn from $16.8-20.8bn; the free-cash-flow add-back rose to $4.1bn from $2.2bn, so reported automotive FCF at the mid-point is about $6.4bn, not $10.5bn.
EV strategic-realignment charges rose from $1,077m (Q1 2026) to $2,279m (Q2 2026) after $7.2bn in Q4 2025; the dossier's 'shrinking sequentially' was wrong.

New 8-K of 11 Aug 2026 (accession 0001193125-26-344698): Master IPU Agreement for up to $4.5bn of supplier-inventory financing recorded as unsecured debt and excluded from adjusted automotive free cash flow until the inventory is purchased; automotive pensions $4.5bn and OPEB $3.9bn ($8.5bn) are also outside the dossier's balance-sheet view.
data_conflicts: V1 rates GM 'excessive' using TTM GAAP EBIT ($1.815bn) and consolidated net debt ($104bn, mostly GM Financial captive debt). Corrected 6 Oct 2026 (RA12): on automotive net cash of $3.67bn (cash $15.15bn + securities $4.50bn - debt $15.98bn at 30 Jun 2026; the $8.7bn in the first version was consolidated) and adjusted automotive free cash flow ($8.0-10.5bn after cash charges and cycle haircut), the corrected reverse DCF (WACC 10.0%) gives implied growth of -3.8% to -7.7% a year, or about -0.7% on the reported guide; V1's 23.5% remains unsupported. The earlier EV/EBIT-adjusted 4.6x/5.0x and -4.6% perpetuity figure treated EBIT as cash and is withdrawn.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: Primary filings were re-read on 6 Oct 2026 (Q2 release combining statements, 10-Q XBRL, 8-K 11 Aug). The cash-flow valuation survives (implied growth below zero on every cash base) but the margin is smaller than first shown, a kill criterion has fired (two quarters of restructuring charges above $1bn), guidance quality is weaker than the headline, and the cycle margin is near a high.

valuation_view_vs_v1.dossier_view: cheap on cash flow, smaller margin than first shown
valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Corrected 6 Oct 2026 (RA12): V1's 23.5% could not be supported (GAAP EBIT depressed by charges, consolidated net debt dominated by GM Financial). The first dossier answer (EV/EBIT-adjusted 4.6x, perpetuity growth near -5%) treated EBIT as cash. Free-cash-flow reverse DCF at WACC 10.0%, EV $72.2bn (market cap $75.19bn - automotive net cash $3.67bn + automotive NCI $0.63bn; $78.6bn with after-tax pension/OPEB): FCF $10.5bn adjusted guide -7.7%; $9.0bn -5.4%; $8.0bn -3.8%; $6.4bn reported guide -0.7%. Central about -3%; evidence-based base 0-2%: implied stays below base, by 3-5 points.

GM.scenario_basis: Annualised 3-year total return from $82.63 on owner free cash flow per share: base FCF $8.0bn flat, buybacks $5.5bn a year, exit 9.0x; bear FCF $4.0bn/$3.0bn/$5.5bn, buybacks $2bn a year, exit 6.5x; bull FCF $11.0bn, buybacks $6.5bn a year, exit 9.0x; dividend $0.72; retained cash kept at par (RA12, own arithmetic; replaces -15% / +9% / +20%).

OMC.thesis_one_line: Now the world's largest ad holding company after merging with Interpublic; cheap on depressed post-merger earnings, but integration is only 10 months old.
kill_criteria: Organic growth (Core Ops) falls below 3% for two consecutive quarters.
Net debt / adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.0x (company net debt was $6.67bn at 30 Jun 2026, about 1.6-1.7x on my estimate; 0.6x pro forma at 31 Dec 2025) at any quarter-end.
Cumulative disclosed 2026 cost synergies come in below $600M (vs the $900M 2026 target) by year-end.
A second consecutive year of full-year GAAP net income below FY2024's $1.48bn level (i.e., integration costs fail to taper as promised).

Any adverse ruling or expanded damages exposure in the A.A. et al v. Omnicom Group Qatar World Cup migrant-labor 'sportswashing' litigation (S.D.N.Y., 1:25-cv-03389; motions to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction denied in 2026) that a reasonable analyst would judge reputationally or financially material.
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 GAAP net loss of $54.5M (EPS -$0.27) driven by merger/integration costs.

Long-term debt roughly doubled to $9.27bn post-merger (from $6.07bn a year earlier); company-defined net debt rose from $2.24bn (31 Dec 2025) to $6.67bn (30 Jun 2026) after $3.0bn of H1 share repurchases (2026 target $3.5bn; 10-Q).
A.A. v. Omnicom Qatar World Cup migrant-labor litigation is proceeding; motions to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction were denied in 2026.
FTC consent order imposes ongoing ad-placement documentation and annual-reporting obligations.
data_conflicts: No V1 row exists for OMC, so no V1 conflict. The triage's extreme trailing P/E (205.8x) and 3,074% EPS-growth figures are confirmed here to be merger-accounting/comp-base noise (FY2025 was a GAAP loss year), not real underlying economics.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: The merger closed only 10 months ago, so no full clean annual comparison exists yet. Net debt/EBITDA and a formal three-closest-peer valuation comp were not independently reconstructed at this depth (disclosed as data gaps in the dossier).

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: [Corrected 2026-10-06 (DVH6)] No V1 valuation row exists for OMC; not applicable. Programme-basis reverse DCF (Ke 8.40% = 5.17% UST + Blume beta 0.781 x 4.14% ERP, ten years then 3.0%, FCF after SBC proxy $2.0-2.7bn from secondary consensus, market cap $21.7bn) implies about -4% to -8% a year of FCF growth, versus organic growth running at 6.1% and a $1.5bn synergy target: implied_vs_base = below. The P/E ~7x heuristic in the dossier is directionally consistent.

WYNN.thesis_one_line: Macau/Las Vegas luxury casino operator riding a genuine mass-market Macau recovery, but carrying elevated, just-repriced-higher debt into an unproven UAE project.
kill_criteria: Net debt / adjusted EBITDAR rises above 4.5x at any quarter-end (from ~3.7-3.9x currently).

Wynn Al Marjan Island opening slips beyond March 2028 (6+ months past the reaffirmed September 2027 date) or total project cost is disclosed at a level requiring new external financing beyond the existing revolvers.
Las Vegas or Encore Boston Harbor adjusted EBITDAR declines YoY for three consecutive quarters (two already logged in Q2 2026).
Macau mass-market table win percentage at either Wynn Palace or Wynn Macau falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters (Wynn Macau was already 15.1-17.1% in the last two quarters - watch closely).
Any credit-rating downgrade following the September 2026 refinancing, or a covenant-headroom disclosure in the next 10-Q.
key_adverse_facts: September 2026 refinancing raised the coupon on $900M of notes from 5.250% to 6.875%, increasing run-rate interest expense.
Las Vegas and Encore Boston Harbor adjusted EBITDAR both declined YoY in Q2 2026.
Wynn Al Marjan Island (UAE) total project cost is undisclosed; cumulative cash contributions were $1.06bn as of Q2 2026 and rising.
Wynn Macau mass-market table win percentage declined YoY in both of the last two quarters (17.1% vs 17.4%; 15.1% vs 18.7%).
data_conflicts: No V1 row exists for WYNN, so no V1 conflict. The triage's cited 5.7x net debt/EBITDA vs our ~3.7-3.9x EBITDAR-basis estimate is most likely a definitional difference (EBITDAR, pre-rent add-back, vs EBITDA, post-rent), not a factual conflict; not independently reconciled at this depth.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: TTM adjusted EBITDAR and net-leverage figures are estimated from a partial (not full 8-quarter) reconstruction, and Wynn Al Marjan Island's total project cost is an undisclosed material unknown that directly affects the leverage/liquidity outlook.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 valuation row exists for WYNN; not applicable. Secondary consensus price targets (~$135, ~66% above the $81.12 close) suggest the market is pricing in more caution than sell-side models - consistent with 'cheap', though the reservation (leverage, undisclosed UAE cost) is why this is INCLUDE-SMALL rather than full INCLUDE. [DV44 2026-10-08: the original text rested on a consensus price target, not a valuation. Free-cash-flow reverse DCF (FCF after SBC and minority about $550M, market cap $8.35bn, 10 years then 3% terminal, cost of equity 10-12%) implies 3.4-7.1% a year (5.3% at 11%) versus delivered H1 EBITDAR +4.2% and revenue +8.0%: in_line, fair not cheap. INCLUDE-SMALL unchanged.]
